standard_prerequisites.name: The distinguished triangle comparing successive reductions
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard consequences of the octahedral axiom, giving the distinguished triangle K tensor I^n/I^{n+1} -> K_{n+1} -> K_n -> K tensor I^n/I^{n+1}[1]
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the triangle along which the induction on n proceeds.

standard_prerequisites.name: Constructibility of the tensor product with a quotient of powers of the ideal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma showing that tensoring a constructible complex over Lambda/I with the constant sheaf on I^n/I^{n+1} stays constructible
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the constructibility of the cohomology of the tensor product appearing in the triangle.

standard_prerequisites.name: Stability of constructible complexes along distinguished triangles
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma that the class of constructible complexes is a Serre subcategory stable under the operations of triangulated categories
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the induction step, since constructibility of the outer terms of the triangle gives it for the middle one.

core_obligations: Set up the reductions (proof lines 5630-5636): put K_n = K tensor over Lambda with the constant sheaf on Lambda/I^n and consider the distinguished triangle relating K_{n+1} and K_n through K tensor I^n/I^{n+1}.

Identify the third term (proof lines 5636-5641): the tensor product K tensor I^n/I^{n+1} equals K_1 tensor over Lambda/I with the constant sheaf on I^n/I^{n+1}, so by the cited lemma its cohomology sheaves are constructible, and vanish when the cohomology of K_1 vanishes.

Induct (proof lines 5641-5645): assuming K_n constructible, the Serre properties of constructible complexes applied to the distinguished triangle give that K_{n+1} is constructible, so the property propagates to all n.
proof_roadmap: Write the comparison of successive reductions as a distinguished triangle.
Identify the third term as a tensor product of the first reduction and conclude constructibility from the cited lemma.
Run the induction using the Serre subcategory properties.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that if the first reduction K tensor Lambda/I of a complex over the pro-etale site is bounded above with constructible cohomology, then so is every reduction modulo a power of the ideal (statement lines 5620-5628). The proof (proof lines 5630-5648) uses the distinguished triangle comparing successive reductions, identifies the third term as a tensor product of the first reduction, and runs an induction using the Serre subcategory properties of constructible complexes. H2: a two-step reduction with three inputs, written out in full.
